paper.title: FORGE: Self-Evolving Agent Memory With No Weight Updates via Population Broadcast
paper.central_claim: A staged, population-based, gradient-free protocol (Reflexion inner loop + champion broadcast + graduation) evolves prompt-injected NL memory so that LLM agents improve over zero-shot (1.7-7.7x) and isolated Reflexion (29-72%) on CybORG CAGE-2 B_line (30 steps) for four LLM families; broadcast is the critical mechanism, graduation mainly saves compute; evidence confined to CAGE-2 B_line.

rationale: 作者报告：champion broadcast 在 CAGE-2 B_line 上优于零样本与 Reflexion；选择与评测分离但同环境、单局探针噪声大、无随机冠军/best-of-N 对照。

evidence.quote: We propose FORGE (Failure-Optimized Reflective Graduation and Evolution), a staged, population-based protocol that evolves prompt-injected natural-language memory for hierarchical ReAct agents.
evidence.support_explanation: Central object: prompt-injected NL memory (not weights) evolved by a staged population protocol.

evidence.quote: no external oracle or stronger model is used
evidence.support_explanation: Same LLM acts and writes memory; no teacher distillation.

evidence.quote: This abort-and-restart cycle converts failures into a structured learning sequence
evidence.support_explanation: Failure-triggered abort -> Reflector/Exemplifier writes Rules/Examples -> artifact appended -> episode restarts (Alg. 1).

evidence.quote: its complete memory state replaces the memory of every other active instance
evidence.support_explanation: Selection/retention rule: argmax of single-episode checkpoint return among non-graduated instances; full destructive replacement of all others.

evidence.quote: Graduation prevents regression by locking strong solutions before the next broadcast cycle can overwrite them, and conserves compute by excluding converged instances from further training.
evidence.support_explanation: Only freeze/lock-in mechanism; the sole 'rollback-like' protection, triggered by one checkpoint episode return > theta=-15.

evidence.quote: To explicitly distinguish selection from reporting, we define two evaluation modes:
evidence.support_explanation: Authors separate checkpoint (selection) from post-session evaluation (reporting).

evidence.quote: a frozen single-episode probe used during training to determine graduation and champion selection
evidence.support_explanation: Selection signal is ONE episode in a stochastic POMDP whose per-instance SDs are 20-90 return units: noisy champion/graduation decisions.

evidence.quote: FORGE improves over both zero-shot and Reflexion baselines for every model family under all three representations
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result vs zero-shot and no-broadcast Reflexion (Table 3).

evidence.quote: FORGE improves post-session evaluation return by 29-72% over Reflexion in all 12 model-representation conditions
evidence.support_explanation: Isolates population broadcast+graduation vs isolated Reflexion under the same inner loop.

evidence.quote: The no-graduation variant also outperforms Reflexion in all 12 conditions, confirming that champion broadcast is the essential mechanism.
evidence.support_explanation: No-graduation ablation; but broadcast = selection + sharing + replication, not separated (no random-champion / best-of-N control).

evidence.quote: The effect of graduation on final performance is model-dependent: removing it helps Grok and Qwen (up to 67% improvement over FORGE, Table
evidence.support_explanation: Graduation's effect on quality is mixed, so 'graduation mainly saves compute' is only partly supported.

evidence.quote: isolated instances can accumulate counterproductive artifacts that degrade performance below the zero-shot starting point
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap: no selection pressure in single-stream Reflexion; Table 3 (Grok Rules/Mixed/Examples Reflexion below zero-shot -58.4) corroborates.

evidence.locator: Table 3 Grok rows; Table 8 Grok rows
evidence.quote_unavailable_reason: Table cell values are split one-per-line in the HTML extraction; no contiguous quote.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3: Grok zero-shot -58.4; Reflexion Rules -79.9, Examples -64.8, Mixed -114.4 (all worse than zero-shot), FORGE -33.7/-42.7/-42.2. Shows isolated-reflection can hurt and broadcast helps.

evidence.quote: brittle single-best broadcast, checkpoint-evaluation misalignment
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede selection brittleness and probe/eval mismatch.

evidence.quote: indicating that the chosen threshold is not optimal and that the broader design space of harsher triggers and multi-threshold triggering remains unexplored.
evidence.support_explanation: Failure-trigger tau sweep: tau=-11 beats the submitted tau=-1.1 (Gemini Rules -24.6 vs -30.6), tau=-2/-3 worse (2 sessions each).

evidence.quote: Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite serves as the primary study model with 7 independent FORGE sessions per representation followed by 1-2 evaluations per instance.
evidence.support_explanation: Replication: 7 sessions for Gemini; 3-4 for others, 2 for no-grad ablation.

evidence.quote: Cross-family findings are presented as directional evidence based on 3-4 sessions per non-Gemini model.
evidence.support_explanation: Scope/statistics caveat acknowledged by authors.

evidence.quote: We therefore adopt Reflexion as the primary baseline and compare it against FORGE under identical model, memory representation, and training budget.
evidence.support_explanation: Only one learned-memory baseline; ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet, TextGrad, ExpeL, CLIN, prompt evolution not run (justified as nontrivial adaptation).

evidence.quote: The no-graduation variants consume more tokens across all representations because all 10 instances remain active for all 6 stages
evidence.support_explanation: Cost reporting incl. per-phase token tables (Table 11) and 12364.0M total tokens (Table 7).

evidence.quote: The magnitude of improvement inversely correlates with baseline strength
evidence.support_explanation: 'Weaker models benefit more' from n=4 models; confounded with ceiling/regression-to-mean.

evidence.quote: broadcast performs full replacement rather than interpolation
evidence.support_explanation: No merge/conflict handling by design; diversity sacrificed.

evidence.quote: with a fixed capacity to prevent unbounded context growth
evidence.support_explanation: Capacity bound stated, but eviction/consolidation policy not described in method text.

evidence.quote: while the Planner has no pre-supplied action knowledge so that any strategic competence it acquires is attributable to learned artifacts
evidence.support_explanation: Information visibility: reflection agents and ActionChooser see the environment action reference table; Planner does not.

evidence.quote: Whereas prompt-evolution methods typically optimize a single monolithic prompt and focus on single-step tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Closest-neighbor positioning (PromptBreeder/EvoPrompt/OPRO) by assertion only; not compared experimentally.

evidence.quote: suggests that the primary bottleneck in prompt-only adaptation is not the quality of individual reflections but the absence of a selection pressure that propagates rare discoveries to the population
evidence.support_explanation: Author interpretation of broadcast gain; alternatives (best-of-N restart, regression to mean) untested.

evidence.quote: although post-session evaluation means remain lower due to sampling variance
evidence.support_explanation: Best checkpoint -3.60 is a selected extreme; authors flag post-session means are much lower (best mean -14.0 to -24.5).

signatures.object: Dynamic prompt memory (Rules / Examples / Mixed) of Planner, Analyst, ActionChooser sub-agents; baseline = empty memory (zero-shot).
signatures.information: Reflector/Exemplifier see the failed trajectory up to the failure step, env state, current memory, and the environment action reference table; only per-step scalar reward is the feedback; no oracle/stronger model.
signatures.operation: Per-step reward < tau=-1.1 aborts episode; same-LLM Reflector writes a conditional heuristic or Exemplifier writes a ReAct demonstration; appended to memory; restart (up to 3 attempts/stage).
signatures.output: Updated memory M_i per instance; after each stage a frozen single-episode checkpoint return R_i.
signatures.conditions: Stochastic POMDP with scalar reward, scripted B_line attacker, 30-step horizon, N=10 instances, S=6 stages.
signatures.feedback: Scalar step reward (failure trigger) + episode return (checkpoint).
signatures.selection_rule: Champion = argmax checkpoint return among non-graduated instances; its full memory replaces all other active memories; instances with R_i > -15 graduate (frozen).
signatures.selection_data: Single frozen checkpoint episode per instance per stage (seeded training environments); reporting uses separate post-session evaluation episodes.
signatures.persistence: Memory files on disk re-injected into system prompts every attempt; fixed capacity; frozen at graduation; final frozen evaluation of all instances.
signatures.later_use: Next-stage attempts and final post-session evaluation episodes (fresh episodes of the same CAGE-2/B_line task).
signatures.claimed_effect: Mean eval return improves 1.7-7.7x over zero-shot and 29-72% over Reflexion in all 12 model-representation conditions; major-failure rate to ~1%.
signatures.failure_boundary: Single attacker/horizon/domain; destructive full replacement; noisy one-episode selection; graduation effect model-dependent; tau not optimal; non-Gemini 3-4 sessions.

gap.author_gap: Single-stream Reflexion in stochastic POMDPs lacks selection pressure and can accumulate counterproductive artifacts; open questions on what to remember, how to propagate memory, and cross-LLM transfer.
gap.checked_gap: Real and partly corroborated in-paper (isolated Reflexion worse than zero-shot for Grok in all three representations; high variance), but the residual is 'select-and-share among parallel Reflexion runs', a PBT-style move over memory; neighbours (ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet, prompt-evolution, ExpeL/CLIN) are discussed but not run, so the improvement over the actual frontier of memory evolvers is unknown.
gap.lineage_closest_adjacent: ReAct -> Reflexion (2023) -> CLIN / ExpeL / Voyager / Dynamic Cheatsheet / ACE (2025) ; PBT (Jaderberg 2017) -> prompt-space PBT; PromptBreeder/EvoPrompt/OPRO for population prompt search (cited in paper, versions as cited). Versions of neighbours not fixed locally (no neighbour full texts in this pack).
gap.residue: Whether gain comes from broadcast per se vs best-of-N selection/replication; no test on other attackers or tasks.
gap.stakes: LLM defenders in CAGE-2 have strongly negative zero-shot returns, so memory improvement is materially useful in-domain.
gap.method_response: Population selection + broadcast replaces isolated updates; graduation freezes converged instances.
gap.remaining_gap: Selection reliability (one-episode probe), diversity loss, cross-environment generalization, comparison with other memory optimizers.
unresolved: Closest neighbors not available as pinned full text in this pack; novelty vs ACE/DC/PBT-prompt methods only by author assertion.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: express new task as conditioning, solve without parameter updates. Domain: failure reflection -> guidance store -> inject into later prompts. Both = condition frozen LLM on stored artifacts written from own experience.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS card expects trained conditioning channel / category holdout; domain card expects contrast, maintenance and gating; FORGE meets grounding and injection, lacks contrast and per-entry maintenance.
